title: Layerwise cast lanes and latency-credit bridge for per-layer mixed-precision
creator: Ethan Cole
description:
Problem: Mixed-precision execution (INT8/FP8/FP16) at per-layer granularity introduces non-trivial casting and dequant overhead during prefill and decode. Two primary pain points have been observed in production traffic: (1) per-layer synchronous cast/unpack stalls that break continuous batching and increase tail latency, and (2) type-mismatch churn between cached KV blocks (often stored in different precisions) and decode kernels that forces repeated conversions. Both effects raise p95/p99 latency and worsen unit cost due to wasted GPU cycles.

Proposed solution: Implement a "Layerwise Cast Lanes" subsystem with a "latency-credit bridge" to amortize and account for cast work across microbatches. Key ideas: (a) Maintain multiple cast lanes per model shard (INT8 lane, FP8 lane, FP16 lane) that hold pre-allocated buffers for converted activations and cached keys; (b) Perform deferred/lazy casting when safe — delay conversion until just before kernel invocation and coalesce casts for batched requests; (c) Introduce a latency-credit accounting mechanism that prefers cheaper paths for latency-sensitive requests and charges credits for heavier conversion work (used by smart routing and fallback); (d) Align cast boundaries to attention slab/stride boundaries so prefill conversions can be reused across similar sequence-prefix traffic; (e) Provide a safe fallback heuristic to use FP16 for layers with observed dynamic range violations or when credit budget is exceeded.

Goals/metrics: Reduce end-to-end p95 decode latency regression from mixed-precision to <= +5% vs FP16 baseline, while improving GPU token throughput for real-world traces by >= 10% in cost-equivalent comparisons. Limit additional memory overhead to <12% per shard for holding layered lanes.

Design notes: Implementation will add a CastLaneManager component inside the serving runtime responsible for: lane buffer lifecycle, lane-specific kernel-launch wrappers, coalescer for pending casts, and a small per-request credit token (integer) that the scheduler can use for routing. The system integrates with existing kernel selector to pick precision-aware kernels and with the KV cache to allocate lane-specific cached views. Interfaces are designed to be low-level JNI/C++ runtime primitives with a thin Rust/Go control-plane binding for rollouts.

Trade-offs: Adds complexity to buffer management and slightly more RAM usage; however avoids repeated ephemeral casts per request and preserves batching efficiency. The latency-credit system complicates routing decisions but enables predictable SLOs for premium traffic.

Rollout plan: Phase 0 (canary): unit tests + microbench harness (local perf and memory). Phase 1 (staged cluster): enable on a small cohort of non-critical models with synthetic traffic and long-prefix cache warmup. Phase 2 (traffic canary): route 5% of production traffic with monitoring dashboards and automated fallback to legacy cast-on-demand path. Phase 3: gradual expansion with per-model tunables (lane memory budget, credit thresholds).
notes_updates: 2026-02-26: Spike completed — measured synchronous cast cost at ~0.9ms per layer on A100 for 128-token decode microbatches; confirmed ordering of casts causes batching fragmentation.
2026-03-02: Design sync with kernel and cache teams. Agreed on an ABI for lane buffers; kernel team to expose 'cast-aware' entrypoints in runtime-1.25 branch.
2026-03-06: Prototype implemented for two-lane (FP16 + INT8) on local harness. Throughput improved 9% on Chat-like traces; p95 latency decreased for batched workloads but p99 unchanged.
2026-03-10: Security review flagged potential info-leak if lane buffers persist across tenant boundaries; decided to enforce zeroing and per-tenant lane isolation for Dedicated/Private deployments.
2026-03-12: Integration tests added. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824 (prototype), design doc uploaded to Confluence.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p95 decode latency for mixed-precision path <= +5% relative to FP16 baseline on representative workloads (chat, instruction, retrieval).
Throughput (tokens/sec) for cost-equivalent runs improves >= 10% vs baseline in at least 2 of 3 workload traces.
No cross-tenant memory exposure; lane buffers zeroed on release and tenant-id namespace enforced for Dedicated/Private.
Automated canary with fallback completes without operational incidents for 72h at 5% production traffic.
Monitoring dashboards and alert runbooks added to Console (latency-credit burn, lane memory, cast error rates).
risks_mitigation: Memory blowup on models with many small layers — mitigation: configurable lane memory caps and LRU reclamation of casted blocks.
Numeric correctness regressions for extreme dynamic range — mitigation: per-layer dynamic-range detector and forced FP fallback plus unit tests with adversarial traces.
Scheduler complexity leading to request starvation — mitigation: soft-credit floor that always preserves a minimal low-latency path for emergency traffic.
Upgrade risk for Private/VPC customers — mitigation: gate feature behind opt-in flag and provide migration guide.
